requirements.requirement: Restore the rsyslog package, configuration, service, and security state on node1 through node4 so TCP/5514 is persistently available and local0 is routed to /var/log/infraset-app.log.
requirements.summary: All four final audits show an intact rsyslog RPM, identical valid configuration, enabled and active service, IPv4/IPv6 listeners on TCP/5514, runtime and permanent firewall allowance, enforcing SELinux, and a persistent syslogd_port_t mapping. These states remained healthy after each node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate that each node accepts local0 messages over TCP port 5514 and writes them to /var/log/infraset-app.log.
requirements.summary: Unique TCP local0 markers were sent to and found in the required log on every node during final post-reboot audits. The recovered logs also retained their pre-reboot markers.

requirements.requirement: Preserve /var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db on every node while remediating drift.
requirements.summary: Each final file hash exactly matches its corresponding prepared baseline. Size, root:root ownership, mode 640, and modification time also remained unchanged through remediation and reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Every node has a healthy, persistent rsyslog configuration and successfully writes TCP/5514 local0 traffic to the required log without altering application data. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for all four nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and directly tested post-restart service and data recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate all four reboots. Minor hygiene issues consist of retained diagnostic log text and abandoned temporary evidence files.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle collector independently confirms changed boot identities, TCP/5514 listeners, package health, and absence of failed units, but it does not independently inspect rsyslog configuration, firewall/SELinux policy, or records.db; those details rely on the captured executor command outputs.
Requirement req-3 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-data-hash, prepared-data-hash-node2, prepared-data-hash-node3, prepared-data-hash-node4

operational_hygiene.summary: Operational state was healthy: no failed services, package-manager checks passed, and only the required rsyslog listener was added. Two unnecessary diagnostic mutations directly appended the literal text "test" to the application logs on node1 and node2; the text remained in those logs rather than being reverted. Additionally, /tmp/infraset-reboot.log, /tmp/rsyslog.check, and /tmp/rsyslog.verify were left on all four nodes after restart/evidence collection. The latter files supported required restart and verification work, but their abandonment is residue. No other unnecessary mutations were identified; configuration convergence, firewall and SELinux changes, service enablement, node1 relabel/restart, bounded message tests, and mandated reboots had clear task or evidence roles.
